title: A comparative retrospective longitudinal study of arthritis risk and cognitive decline in older adults.
figures: Kaplan–Meier survival curve of the proportion of total participants remaining without an arthritis diagnosis over a 12-year period. The number of participants at risk at 0, 24, 48, 72, 96, 120, 144, and 168 months is shown below the survival curves.

Kaplan–Meier analysis curves by sex and cognitive function, illustrating the proportion of participants remaining without an arthritis diagnosis over a 12-year period. The lines represent the following groups: blue solid line = man with normal cognition, blue dashed line = man with cognitive decline, red solid line = woman with normal cognition, and red dashed line = woman with cognitive decline.
tables: Baseline characteristics of participants by cognitive function.
Risk factors for arthritis in total participants ( N  = 1,142).
Risk factors for arthritis in older adults with cognitive decline ( n  = 334) and normal cognition ( n  = 808).
